LeaveBalanceGrantIn.description:
Post a credit to one employee's ledger — a grant, an accrual, or a plain adjustment.

`idempotency_key` is optional but strongly encouraged: without one, a retried request (a
client timeout, a double-click) posts a second credit, because there is nothing here for the
server to recognise as "the same request" (CLAUDE.md's idempotency rule applies to this
write exactly as it does to a payment).

get.description:
`employee_id` is required, not optional — the one thing that keeps this endpoint bounded
without a page parameter (CLAUDE.md: no unbounded list query). One employee's balances are at
most the handful of leave types an organization defines; "every employee's balance" is
deliberately not a read this endpoint offers in this slice — an ORG-scoped caller asking for
it would otherwise return one row per employee per type with nothing to page it by. `ctx.apply`
still narrows an OWN-scoped caller to their own id regardless of what they pass here.

post.description:
Self-service (ADR-0006). Opens a `pending` request and publishes
`hrms.time.leave.requested`; approval routes it and reports the decision back on
`core.approval.request.decided`, applied by `app.consumers`.

The documented escape hatch (ADR-0006 §6) — HR cancels a stuck or mistaken request
directly, audited in its own domain, without going through approval. `ctx` here is already
guarded at `minimum=Scope.ORG`, so no object-level identity check is needed: an ORG-scoped
caller may touch any employee's request by construction (`ScopeContext.assert_can_touch`).
post.summary: Cancel any employee's leave request directly (HR override)

get.description:
Route traffic on this; restart on /health.

Conflating the two restarts a healthy process that is merely waiting on a
dependency.

Only the dependencies a service actually declares are checked. A gateway owns no
tables, so asking it for a database is asking a question whose answer means nothing
— and a readiness probe that reports on something the service does not use is worse
than no probe, because it will eventually fail for a reason nobody can act on.

Reachable only on the compose `back` network (`tests/infra`'s
`test_metrics_never_routed.py` is the lint that keeps it that way) — never behind
Caddy or a gateway, the same rule `ops_monitor`'s own `/metrics` follows.

`db_pool_in_use` is always reported when this service has a database; the three
outbox gauges only when `outbox_model` is configured — same gate as `/health/outbox`,
and the same reason: an app-role connection with no tenant bound sees zero rows.
